findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves, in plain words. This part works well.
findings.source: Header lede: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The only section meant to show Athena's own output (models, verdict, cost) shows an internal error instead, and it sits second on the page. A newcomer sees a broken promise right after the pitch and gets no proof of the cost and verdict tracking the lede describes.
findings.source: Check it on a real job: "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: Apart from three intro paragraphs and Next steps, the whole page is a detailed study of a different project, firstmate. The intro does explain this, but a newcomer who came to learn about Athena has to wade through a long state-machine reference that is not about Athena.
findings.source: Title "Athena explains how firstmate handles work" and the sections States, Counters, Transitions, Claims and sources

findings.text: The firstmate study is easy to approach: it defines terms before using them and gives a one-sentence summary and a step-by-step walk through one task. A reader who wants firstmate's design can follow it.
findings.source: Start here, "Words used first" and "What firstmate is"

findings.text: This link speaks to the site's owner, not a visitor, and appears at the top beside the newcomer's next-step link. It is likely to confuse a first-time reader.
findings.source: Header: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: The next steps are concrete: prerequisites, a clone command, a setup script and a first command to try. A newcomer knows what to do next, and a link to the Athena repository is also in the header.
findings.source: Next steps: "Before installing, have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm" ... "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: Several glossary entries say the term is undefined instead of defining it. That is honest, but a newcomer is left with words they cannot pin down.
findings.source: Glossary entries such as "The firstmate source does not define a heartbeat." and "The firstmate source does not define an endpoint."
